_meta.note: Reusable IDENTIFIER LAYER (dishwasher POC): observed catalogue identifier -> canonical technical model -> OEM platform. Kept SEPARATE from error-code definitions so the resolver can do identifier-resolution BEFORE scheme resolution. Data-only; not wired into production.

identifierClasses.TECHNICAL_MODEL: resolvable to OEM/platform directly (e.g. WQP12-9368, DW12SAE, BFSLNB9B)
identifierClasses.RETAILER_SKU: opaque 7-10 digit internal/retailer stock number (e.g. 5500064976) - NOT resolvable from public web in this POC
identifierClasses.MARKETING_MODEL: brand marketing name; may or may not encode platform
identifierClasses.MALFORMED: too short/numeric to be a model

keyFindings: Retailer SKU -> technical model is NOT recoverable at scale from public sources: searching the exact 10-digit 5500xxxxx SKU returns only generic brand manuals, never the specific model.
Parts cross-check does NOT bridge SKU->model here: the SKU's parts (8-digit part numbers) share no PCB/controller with the WQP models (14-digit part numbers).

Where the catalogue already stores a TECHNICAL model, platform resolution works and reveals that ONE BADGE SPANS MULTIPLE OEM LINEAGES: Bush DW = WQP* (Midea-family) + DW*/DWFS* (a different family) + BFS* (another).
Therefore identifier resolution must key on the TECHNICAL MODEL; SKU rows require a retailer-provided SKU<->model feed (not public).
